summary_1line: Bhishma teaches that detachment, ethical conduct, disciplined speech and senses, and yogic self‑control lead to knowledge of the Self and final emancipation.

image_candidates.scene_text: An austere mendicant sits in solitude, eyes closed, while the five senses symbolically withdraw into his mind like rays returning to the sun.
A yogi living on sparse alms—roots, grains, and fruits—meditates beneath a tree as the sun slowly rises, symbolizing Brahman gradually shining within.
Robbers hurriedly dropping stolen sheep on a dark road to escape the king’s watch, symbolizing the casting off of passions and sinful acts.
